Butterflies are loud, bold, and impossible to miss. So why are they so hard to catch?
A new Nature study says those stripes are a trick played on motion.
Zebra stripes were long suspected of the same thing. Proof was thin.
So researchers filmed take-offs at a thousand frames per second, and compared them with digital butterflies with blank wings.
With real patterns, flapping wings sent false signals. A butterfly flying upward could look, to predator vision, like it was moving down.
Across 397 European species, bold forewings, vertical stripes and hindwing tails added the most confusion.
A computer even evolved 57,600 wing patterns for confusion, and it landed on butterfly-like designs.
And volunteers chasing virtual butterflies on a touchscreen aimed behind them, as if they were slower than they were.
The flash that gives a butterfly away may be what saves it. Latoon. Voyaging the unseen. Follow for more.
